lead.claim: Intermittent hypoxia may boost ankle strength and walking in MS.
lead.context: Why this matters: A randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled crossover trial investigated whether acute intermittent hypoxia improves motor function in people with multiple sclerosis.

supporting.claim: Can oropharyngeal exercises help swallowing with limited mouth opening?
supporting.context: Why this matters: A pilot study explored the feasibility and initial effects of oropharyngeal alignment exercise on swallowing function in neurological patients with restricted mouth opening.

supporting.claim: Education, BMI, and academy training predict elite distance running.
supporting.context: Why this matters: An observational study identified factors beyond physiology that may contribute to high performance in Ethiopian distance runners.
